answer: A secure enclave attestation protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical cryptoprocessors. Nodes must maintain an authenticated attestation thread that signs randomized challenges within a strict timeout horizon, modulated by a velvet noise sequence. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of purchasing dedicated, certified hardware enclaves per identity. However, side-channel vulnerabilities can expose root signing keys, enabling adversaries to spoof attestations.
